source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: What is an essay outline? Prepare an outline for an essay on 'Federalism in Nepal'.
questions.solution:
An **outline** is the skeleton plan — headings in logical order — written before drafting.

**Model outline:** I. Introduction (2015 constitution, 7 provinces). II. Advantages (inclusion, local development, identity). III. Challenges (cost, capacity, disputes). IV. Conclusion (cooperative federalism as the way forward).
questions.knowledgeNote: Outlines prevent rambling — examiners reward visible planning even before reading the essay.

questions.question: What are cohesive devices? Give two examples each of addition, contrast, and cause-effect linkers.
questions.solution:
**Cohesive devices** (linkers) glue sentences into flowing text.

**Addition:** moreover, furthermore. **Contrast:** however, on the other hand. **Cause-effect:** therefore, consequently. (Time: meanwhile, subsequently; example: for instance.)
questions.knowledgeNote: One linker per 2–3 sentences is the natural density — more feels mechanical, fewer feels choppy.

questions.question: What is a topic sentence? Write a topic sentence for a paragraph on 'Importance of English'.
questions.solution:
The **topic sentence** states a paragraph's single controlling idea, usually first.

**Example:** 'English opens doors to global education, employment, and information that no other single language can.' — every following sentence must serve this claim (unity).
questions.knowledgeNote: Stray sentences break unity — the fastest way to lose paragraph marks.

questions.question: Distinguish between formal and informal letter formats with examples of salutation and closing for each.
questions.solution:
**Formal** (editor, principal): subject line, 'Dear Sir/Madam,' … 'Yours faithfully,' — full names, no contractions.

**Informal** (friends, family): no subject, 'Dear Sita,' … 'Your loving friend,' — warm tone, contractions fine.
questions.knowledgeNote: Matching the register to the recipient is itself a marked skill — wrong tone, lost marks.

questions.question: What are the qualities of a good summary? Write any four.
questions.solution: (1) **Complete** — all main ideas, nothing essential dropped. (2) **Concise** — about one-third length. (3) **Coherent** — logical flow in own words. (4) **Objective** — no personal views or new examples.
questions.knowledgeNote: Summary vs précis: same discipline — précis is the stricter, examination-formatted cousin.

questions.question: Correct the subject-verb agreement errors: (a) 'The list of items are long.' (b) 'Neither of the boys have come.' (c) 'Mathematics are difficult.'
questions.solution: (a) 'The list of items **is** long.' — the verb follows 'list', not 'items'. (b) 'Neither of the boys **has** come.' — neither/either take singular verbs. (c) '**Mathematics is** difficult.' — -ics subjects (mathematics, physics, news) are singular.
questions.knowledgeNote: Find the true subject by ignoring prepositional phrases between it and the verb.
